title: Design predictive survival engine for Minecraft 26.1.2
objective: Produce an implementation-ready design for a Minecraft Java 26.1.2 Fabric/Meteor client module that predicts observable incoming damage using vanilla-faithful mechanics and chooses server-valid survival actions, including correctly timed totem use, without assuming unverified exploits.
acceptance_criteria: The design targets Minecraft Java 26.1.2 and Java 25 and uses the supplied 26.1.2 source as the behavioral source of truth

The design reproduces the vanilla player/living-entity damage pipeline, hurt cooldown and lastHurt semantics, armor/toughness, effects, enchantments, absorption, blocking, damage tags, and death protection in the correct order

The design defines predictors for explosions, projectiles, melee and mace threats, falls, environmental hazards, status/tick damage, and other observable vanilla damage families with explicit confidence and timing semantics

The design defines a server-authoritative action planner covering totems, shielding, cover placement, movement/evasion, equipment changes, instant effects, fall clutches, escape actions, and only mathematically beneficial hurt-cooldown manipulation
The design accounts for shield warmup, inventory/offhand/mainhand synchronization, ping and server-tick uncertainty, and rejects client-only desync as protection
Every speculative or exploit-like survival tactic is gated behind feasibility simulation and runtime verification rather than being assumed to work
Architecture boundaries, data flow, error/fallback behavior, performance limits, settings, observability, and a deterministic testing strategy are explicit
The written spec contains no TODO/TBD placeholders or contradictory requirements and is ready to feed into an implementation plan after human review
